column1: # MUST_CONTAIN.tsv -- the BOM for v1.0.68.
# THIS FILE IS THE SOURCE. CM051 VENDORS IT.
# CM051 scripts/sync_cut_bom.sh copies this file into cuts/v1.0.68/ there and
# records the OS003 commit it came from in cuts/BOM_PIN. Authoring it in CM051
# instead produces a copy with no pin, "a fork nobody declared".
# EVERY ROW SAYS ONE OF THREE THINGS AND NEVER A FOURTH
#   gate:<workflow>#<what>  a CI gate that FAILS on the real pre-fix tree
#   artefact:<sha8>#<what>  measured on the published artefact itself
#   needs-walk:<ver>#<what> UNPROVEN, and here is exactly what to look at
# WHY THIS CUT EXISTS, IN ONE LINE
# v1.0.67 was cut, published, installed CLEAN (38 of 38 steps, 0 errors) and
# walked FOUR TIMES on archie@192.168.1.240, ending 16 pass / 6 fail / 2
# cannot-run. Its artefact sha256 never changed across those walks. EVERY FIX
# MERGED SINCE ITS PIN IS THEREFORE UNWALKED, and there are eight of them --
# six in install.sh, one in the vendored ostler_fda, one in the install
# manifest. v1.0.68 exists to put those on a box.
# WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT A ROW HERE, SO THE ABSENCE IS DECLARED
# CM051 35fb1a41 (#1505) changed install.sh and gets NO row. It rejoins a
# sentence #1503 split and deletes two line-number citations that had already
# rotted. It is prose inside a comment block: it adds no capability, changes no
# branch, and there is nothing a gate could fail on for the pre-fix tree. A BOM
# is a MUST-CONTAIN list, not a changelog, and inventing a verify column for a
# comment would put an unfalsifiable row next to seven falsifiable ones.
# It rides the cut; it is not proven by it. That is the honest statement.
# The other eighteen commits since 03b50c6b are walks, walk-harness fixes,
# tests and docs. None of them reach the DMG payload, so none can be a row.
# LANDED, AND HOW THAT WAS ESTABLISHED
# Every ref below is an ANCESTOR of f60307ad, which is the CM051 pin this cut
# is built from -- checked with `git merge-base --is-ancestor <ref> f60307ad`,
# not asserted. Ancestry is valid in ONE direction only: TRUE proves landed.
# EVERY `gate:` ROW WAS EXECUTED AGAINST THE PRE-FIX TREE. ONE FAILED TO.
# Claiming a gate "fails on the pre-fix tree" is a claim, and TEST_WIRING.tsv
# proves a test is WIRED, not that it can FAIL. So each was run against
# install.sh at 03b50c6b, the v1.0.67 pin, with the fixed tree as the control:
#   #1500 plistbuddy exit code          rc=1  FAILS pre-fix
#   #1506 install manifest              rc=1  FAILS pre-fix
#   #1495 store health foreign port     rc=2  CANNOT-RUN pre-fix
#   #1512 uninstall removal honesty     rc=2  CANNOT-RUN pre-fix
#   #1503 hydrate cap floors            RED   1 failure over 10 caps
#   #1511 projection prune              5 arms, 3 must-miss, mutation-tested
#   #1498 port preflight                rc=0  PASSES -- DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE
#   CONTROL: all seven return rc=0 on the fixed tree, so a pre-fix non-zero is
#            the change and not a broken harness.
# THE TWO CANNOT-RUNs ARE ACCEPTED AS EVIDENCE AND THE REASON IS NARROW. Both
# refuse because the thing they extract BY NAME did not exist before the fix
# (_ostler_store_container_is_ours; the uninstaller teardown marker). A gate
# that refuses is a gate that would block a regression, and rc=2 is a refusal,
# never a pass. It is weaker evidence than rc=1 and is recorded as such rather
# than rounded up.
# #1498 IS THEREFORE needs-walk, NOT gate. Its own test returns 16 pass / 0 fail
# on the pre-fix tree: it tests preflight COVERAGE and the bind probe, while the
# fix swapped `fail` for `fail_with_code`. Rather than let the row wear a gate
# that cannot fail for it, the row says what to look at on the box.
what

THE PEOPLE PROJECTION MUST REMOVE AS WELL AS ADD. ingest_people_to_qdrant was a one-way projection: a Person that left the graph kept its vector for ever. MEASURED ON THE v1.0.67 WALK: doctor reported 1907 people, oxigraph held 1823, and the 84-point difference was exactly the orphan count, every one of them source=fda_people_index. Two walk probes failed on one defect. The prune only ever runs off a SUCCESSFUL projection, a failed read prunes nothing, and it deletes nothing it did not write.

THE STORE HEALTH ARMS REPORTED HEALTHY ON ANOTHER ACCOUNT'S CONTAINER. Same class as the v1.0.66 ollama finding and found by looking for its siblings: a bare loopback probe cannot tell whose service answered. On a shared Mac the arms went green while the walked account had nothing listening at all. REACHABLE IS NOT OURS.

THE READINESS BUDGET THAT FAILED THE COLD WALK WAS INVISIBLE TO ITS OWN FLOOR GATE. _QDRANT_COLLECTIONS_READY_CAP was written so the discovery regex could not see it: 10 caps discoverable, this one 0 of 10, so NEITHER the below-floor arm NOR the undeclared arm reached the one budget that actually blew. cm019_setup went ERROR at 132s against a 120s cap on the cold walk. VERIFIED BY EXECUTION 2026-09-05: the fixed gate run against install.sh at the v1.0.67 pin reports 1 failure over 10 caps (MISSING _QDRANT_COLLECTIONS_READY_CAP); against this tree it is clean at 11 of 11, and --self-test exits 0.

THE TWO PORT-PREFLIGHT ABORTS GAVE THE CUSTOMER NO SUPPORT CODE. An install that stops because a port is taken is the single most likely thing to happen on a Mac that already runs something, and it stopped with prose nobody can quote at support. MEASURED, AND THIS ROW IS DELIBERATELY needs-walk RATHER THAN gate: the test #1498 shipped alongside itself, test_port_preflight_covers_published.sh, returns 16 pass / 0 fail AGAINST THE PRE-FIX TREE at 03b50c6b. It tests preflight COVERAGE and the bind probe; the fix swapped fail for fail_with_code. The test is good and it is not this row evidence.
column6: needs-walk:v1.0.68#install.sh port_preflight -- force a collision on 8144 and confirm the abort banner carries ERR-06-PORTS-HELD, then make netstat unavailable and confirm ERR-06-PORT-PREFLIGHT-CANNOT-RUN. Two DISTINCT codes; one code for both is the defect.

column1: A PLISTBUDDY READ MUST TAKE ITS OWN EXIT CODE. The upgrade path read the service token through PlistBuddy and threw the status away, so a failed read was indistinguishable from a token that was legitimately absent.
THE UNINSTALLER MUST NOT ANNOUNCE A REMOVAL IT DID NOT DO. It printed removal lines unconditionally, so a customer who ran it and kept their data was told the opposite of what happened.

THE MANIFEST MUST DECLARE WHAT THE INSTALL ACTUALLY PRODUCES. It required com.ostler.enrich, an agent this install deliberately does not create, and omitted com.creativemachines.ostler.context-refresh, which it does. A manifest that asks for the wrong things fails honest installs and passes broken ones.
